messages.author: e7a185e1c89c24a2
messages.subject: control the shape of points in a scatter plot
parts:
I have worked out the following lines of code:

#-------------------------------------------------------

# set chart
ggplot(data, aes(tv.avg, ped.avg, colour=composto))+

# diagonal line
geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1)+

# points: this is not working!
geom_point(aes(colour=composto, shape=composto), size=2.5)+

# label position
#geom_text(aes(label=composto, x = tv.avg, y = ped.avg),
colour="black", size=2.5, hjust=0, vjust=0)+

# x axis
scale_x_log10(name="treviso",
limits=c(1,10000),breaks=c(1,10,100,1000,10000),formatter="scientific")
+

# y axis
scale_y_log10(name="pederobba", limits=c(1,10000),
breaks=c(1,10,100,1000,10000),formatter="scientific")+

opts(title=paste("CD =", cd, sep=" "), legend.position="right",
legend.title="composto")+

# background
theme_bw(base_size = 10)+

# scale_colour
scale_colour_hue("composto", h=c(0, 180))

# ----------------------------------------------

my problem now is how to deal with the need to shape the points when
you have more than 6 discrete values (in my case are 29!);
I've been reading on the help page about a possibility with the use of
scale_manual but i can't figure how: any help for this?

thank you for any support (sorry about the trivial question but I'm a
new user)
max

messages.subject: Re: control the shape of points in a scatter plot
parts:
Max, you have to use the value argument. The value argument only accepts integers that are related to the shape. However 29 shapes is to much to make sense of it. I think there are only 20 or so distinct shapes. The rest are shapes that can be filled.
Luciano

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: control the shape of points in a scatter plot
parts: Hi,

> With 29 different categories I would try to facet so that you have sets of
> data types in different panels perhaps. 29 would be hard to make sense of in
> one plot

or, text symbolization may be useful, I don't recommend though.

d <- data.frame(x=rnorm(29), y=rnorm(29), v=factor(1:29))

# shape version
ggplot(d, aes(x,y)) + geom_point(aes(shape=v)) + scale_shape_manual(values=1:29)

# text version
ggplot(d, aes(x,y)) + geom_text(aes(label=c(letters, LETTERS)[v]))

--

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: control the shape of points in a scatter plot
parts:
> can you show me how you wold deal with this problem?
> I perfectly know that working with 29 categories it's quite hard and
> somehow does not make any sense but for a number of reasons I do not
> mention here I have to and therefore I need to find the best solution
> for this problem

I think the best you can do is to label the points directly:

ggplot(data, aes(tv.avg, ped.avg))+
geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1) +

geom_point(size=2.5) +
geom_text(aes(label = composto), hjust = 0) +
scale_x_log10() +
scale_y_log10()

But it really needs a lot of hand tweaking for readability.

Hadley
